thread:
incident-bot: 

🔔 ALERT: Elevated 5xx and latency from inference-hosts in us-west-2a. 5xx ~= 18% over 3m, P99 token latency spike ~950ms. Affected endpoints: /v1/chat, /v1/generate. Pager: @oncall-sre. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/az-network-degen>

oncall-sre: I've got the page. Starting triage: pulling NLB target health, instance system logs, and LB access logs. Tagging net and infra.

jen: support queue shows multiple customers reporting "502 downstream" and session disconnects. Two Dedicated pools in us-west-2a are showing repeated healthcheck failures.

rafael: looking at cloudwatch: NLB health checks for targets in us-west-2a show consecutive "HTTP 502" responses and connection resets. Instance system logs show `ensX: tx timeout` and `eth0: link down` on some hosts.

net-sre: we see bursty packet drops and TX errors on the ENIs in us-west-2a. Also seeing control-plane throttles when our control plane attempts fast re-registers of targets after deregistration. Likely a mix of host NIC flakiness + ENI attach/detach rate limits.

infra-lead: important: we have scheduled a minor autoscaler job in us-west-2a that started 6m ago. Pause any automated scaling/deploy ops in that AZ.

oncall-sre: mitigation plan: (A) divert traffic away from us-west-2a by changing Route53 weights and our internal router; (B) pause rollout and autoscaling in affected AZ; (C) cordon and graceful drain worst nodes; (D) open case with AWS and request ENI attach-rate investigation; (E) escalate customer comms. Execute in that order.

jen: starting customer comms: "We're investigating elevated errors in us-west-2. Mitigation in progress. We will share ETA in 30 minutes."

deploy-bot: auto-rollout paused per policy: found 3 in-progress rollouts in cluster-usw2; action=paused.

rafael: applying Route53 change now to shift weight away from us-west-2a. TTL is low (60s) so should propagate quickly. Command: ```bash
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZZZ --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.ai","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"us-west-2a","Weight":0,"TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"1.2.3.4"}]}}]}'
```

net-sre: also patching regional router to mark us-west-2a disabled for new sticky sessions. `kubectl -n infra patch cm regional-router -p '{"data":{"us-west-2a":"disabled"}}'`

infra-lead: setting ASG desired capacity in us-west-2b/c up + scaling policies to absorb diverted traffic. `aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name infra-usw2b --desired-capacity 24`

support-ops: notifying enterprise contacts and creating urgent tickets for Dedicated customers pinned to us-west-2a. Flagging potential SLA impact if error rate persists beyond 60m.

aws-support-bot: Case opened: 9876543210. AWS acknowledges region-level network plane anomalies in us-west-2a and is investigating ENI attach errors and host NIC metrics. ETA unknown.

jen: updating status page to "Partial service degradation: some requests routing to us-west-2a may see errors. Traffic steering in progress." Posting to status.redwood.ai

oncall-sre: draining nodes in us-west-2a slowly to avoid kV cache stampede. Command: `kubectl drain node/node-abc --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120`

net-sre: note: when draining, kvcache mis-warms cause transient P50 jump. We will stagger drains by AZ and by pool. Also enabling in-memory warmup on new nodes to reduce cold tails.

rafael: after weight shift, 5xx dropped from 18% -> 6% within two minutes. P99 latency fell from 950ms -> 220ms. Some clients still failing due to long-lived connections to unhealthy targets; NLB connection draining will clear in TTL window.

deploy-bot: detected a deployment that would have re-registered targets in us-west-2a; blocked automatically.

infra-lead: paused scheduled reboots and maintenance in us-west-2a. Adding hold on any infra jobs.

support-ops: customer update sent: "Routing adjusted to mitigate errors. We'll reach out to impacted enterprise customers directly in parallel."

oncall-sre: handing page to @rafael for ongoing monitoring and AWS coordination. I'll take 20 for relief.

rafael: ack. continuing watch. if 5xx > 5% for next 30m, we will consider cross-region failover to eu-west-1 for critical traffic and apply model throttles to reduce retry amplification.

aws-support-bot: AWS update: observed elevated ENI TX errors and a subset of host NICs reporting driver resets. Engineers are correlating host firmware and network fabric telemetry. Recommended mitigation: keep traffic off the AZ and avoid rapid ENI attach/detach.

net-sre: suggested long-term change: reduce ephemeral ENI churn during scale events and implement local target sticky caching to avoid frequent re-register flaps. Adding item to infra backlog.

jen: posting timeline to status: T+0m alert; T+5m route shift; T+10m node drains; T+15m errors down to 6%; T+30m monitoring.

incident-bot: ACTIONS LOGGED: route_shift; asg_scale_out=us-west-2b,us-west-2c; node_drains_started; aws_case=9876543210; deployments_paused.

rafael: monitoring shows errors holding ~4% after 20m steady state. Some Dedicated customers with pinned pools still seeing degraded throughput — support-ops is opening priority remediation tickets to move those pools.

support-ops: remedied one dedicated pool by reassigning its instances to us-west-2b; IBMCorp contact notified. Two other accounts requested manual scheduling; we've taken offline steps and informed them of temporary capacity hits.

infra-lead: reminder for post-incident: collect core dumps from affected hosts, preserve instance metadata, and capture ENI attach/detach traces. Do not terminate instances until AWS asks for them.

net-sre: small gotcha: due to short TTLs we used, some DNS caches rebalanced quickly but mobile clients with long-lived connections saw residual failures. We'll document a graceful connection drain note for customers.

rafael: AWS now indicates root-cause likely a combination of NIC driver resets on some host types + ENI attach API throttling under churn. They will provide telemetry dump in RCA.

jen: external update: "Mitigation applied; errors reduced. Investigating root cause with cloud provider. Post-incident RCA to follow."

incident-bot: RESOLUTION CHECK: current 5xx ~= 1.5% (baseline ~1%). Latency near baseline. Keeping incident open for RCA & evidence collection.

rafael: leaving detailed incident notes in tracker and handing to next oncall at 3098783500. We'll reconvene for RCA conference in 2 hours.

support-ops: will follow up with all affected customers with timeline and next steps. Closing external comms loop after RCA posted.

infra-lead: action items assigned: (1) net-sre -> implement ENI-churn detection alert; (2) infra -> audit autoscaler trigger patterns and reduce simultaneous attaches; (3) eng -> add automated AZ-steer in runbook when ENI attach errors exceed threshold.

oncall-sre: thanks everyone. moving to postmortem.
